title: A tutoring promise built for the US.
shortTitle: Earning trust in a new tutoring market.
description: A successful marketplace playbook did not automatically fit a new market. I used student research to shape US-specific matching around collaborative learning and a clear promise on response time.
trust: Trust mechanism: a 60-second matching promise, kept for 98% of US requests in under 45.
scope: I owned the US launch across matching, activation, OCR intake, and the session experience. I worked with engineering, data science, and operations on student and tutor workflows.
heroCaption: The marker shows the measured matching result against the target. Individual step durations are not implied.

decision.over: Port the existing India matching model.
decision.evidence: 100+ user interviews informed the US experience.
decision.tradeoff: Adapt the matching and session experience instead of reusing the existing playbook unchanged.
decision.cost: Dedicated work on US matching, onboarding, and session continuity.

sections.label: The Problem
sections.title: A working playbook still needed a local test.
paragraphs: Filo had 2M+ users when I joined. The existing marketplace provided a starting point, but bringing it to the US required understanding whether its matching experience met local student expectations.

sections.label: What I Found
sections.title: Students wanted to learn together.
paragraphs: Across 100+ user interviews, collaborative learning emerged as a key need for the US experience. That called for more than translating the interface. Matching, onboarding, and the session itself needed to support that expectation.

sections.label: What Shipped
sections.title: Make the promise visible in the request path.
paragraphs: The experience connected uploaded problems, OCR intake, US-specific matching, tutor acceptance, and a live session. Matching had a 60-second target. Session continuity and low-bandwidth audio/video supported the experience after the match.
I worked across the activation funnel and student and tutor onboarding, with quality thresholds and fraud detection supporting marketplace trust.

sections.label: Outcomes
sections.title: A US marketplace with a promise it could keep.
paragraphs: The US marketplace went on to reach 120K users and $1.5M ARR in six months. 98% of US requests matched in under 45 seconds against a 60-second target.

sections.label: What I Learned
sections.title: Local insight belongs in the core product.
paragraphs: Market entry is a product decision, not just a distribution decision. Trust came from adapting the experience to how students wanted to learn and then delivering on a measurable promise.
